nodes.content: Develop informative treatment-effect confidence sets when confounding proxies are weak and their conditional independence assumptions are approximately violated.
requirements: Guarantee at least 95% asymptotic coverage uniformly over explicitly quantified proxy-strength and assumption-violation classes.
Characterize when confidence sets are strictly narrower than outcome-range-only bounds without requiring point identification.

nodes.content: Invert slack-adjusted Anderson–Rubin proxy moments at 95% uniformly over δ≤0.05 conditional-independence violations and zero-strength proxies; tighten via positive endpoint margins.
When do profiled proxy moments exclude both outcome-range endpoints after δ-slack, even as proxy singular values approach zero?
Proxy-moment gaps at both endpoints exceeding δ plus the 95% critical radius yield strict bound tightening, even with rank-deficient proxies.
Derive uniformly calibrated 95% inversion and compute profiled endpoint margins across proxy strengths 0–0.2 and violations δ≤0.05.
Run 10,000 Monte Carlo replications per cell (n=1,000; proxy singular value 0–0.2; δ=0–0.05), recording coverage and endpoint exclusion.
ProxyGrid-v1 tabulates treatment-effect coverage, confidence-set width, and endpoint exclusion across 10,000-replication strength–δ cells at n=1,000.
Stratify ProxyGrid-v1 by whether both endpoint gaps exceed δ plus the 95% critical radius; test strict tightening in zero-strength cells.
In ProxyGrid-v1 zero-strength cells, 18% exceeded both endpoint-gap thresholds yet retained width 2.0 (binary outcomes) through unbounded bridges.
For bridges bounded by 5, both profiled endpoint gaps exceeding δ plus critical radius ensure tightening at zero strength.
Reanalyze ProxyGrid-v1 imposing |bridge|≤5; check whether threshold-qualified zero-strength cells tighten, and report 95% coverage across δ≤0.05.
With |bridge|≤5, all threshold-qualified zero-strength ProxyGrid-v1 cells narrowed below 2.0; minimum simulated coverage over δ≤0.05 was 95.1%.
Adopt |bridge|≤5 instead of unrestricted bridges: zero-strength endpoint tightening occurred without observed coverage loss.
Derive worst-case AR critical values and prove ≥95% uniform asymptotic coverage for |bridge|≤5, δ≤0.05, proxy strengths 0–0.2.
With |bridge|≤5 and bounded, nondegenerate moments, Gaussian-max calibration proves ≥95% uniform asymptotic coverage for strengths 0–0.2, δ≤0.05.
Can auxiliary validation data justify |bridge|≤5 when proxies have zero strength, preserving the uniform 95% coverage guarantee?
Independent validation certifying bridge norm ≤5 at 97.5% confidence enables 97.5% AR inversion with ≥95% coverage, including zero-strength proxies.
Use LP-relaxed latent mixtures with δ≤0.05 proxy-independence violations and simultaneous 95% multinomial bands; dual bounds certify narrowing without inversion.
Calibrate 95% multinomial bands; establish uniform LP coverage at strengths 0–0.2 and δ≤0.05; derive dual conditions for strict tightening.
Apply 95%-band LP and bounded-bridge AR sets to ProxyGrid-v1; compare minimum coverage, median width, and endpoint exclusion.
ProxyGrid-v1 TV-stress (δ=0.04) caused bridge drift 0.20: LP covered 95.3%; moment-slack AR had 0% limiting coverage.
Adopt LP for TV-bounded violations; retain proved AR coverage only under moment-space δ or bridge-adjusted TV slack.
Implement n22’s LP-primary, AR-moment-only policy; prove 95% uniform LP coverage for TV δ≤0.05, strengths 0–0.2; derive dual certificates.
ProxyLP-v1 documents LP-primary/AR-moment-only rules, uniform 95% LP coverage for TV δ≤0.05 and strengths 0–0.2, and dual tightening certificates.
Does ProxyLP-v1 retain endpoint exclusion and 95% coverage when latent-class discretization grows beyond two classes at zero proxy strength?
If K-class approximation error ≤εK, εK-inflated LP bands preserve ≥95% coverage; positive adjusted dual margins exclude zero-strength endpoints.
Stress-test ProxyLP-v1 at K=2,4,8 and zero proxy strength; inflate bands by certified εK and measure coverage and endpoint exclusion.
At K=2,4,8 and δ≤0.05, εK-inflated ProxyLP-v1 attained ≥95.1% zero-strength coverage; positive bilateral dual margins excluded both endpoints.
Extend the LP-primary policy to K=2,4,8 with certified εK inflation; report strict narrowing only with positive bilateral dual margins.
Can audited TV-radius upper bounds replace fixed δ=0.05 in ProxyLP-v1 without losing uniform coverage at zero strength?
Independently certify TV radii and |bridge|≤5 at 97.5%; separately invert LP/AR at 97.5% and test zero-strength coverage.
Independent 97.5% bridge certification plus 97.5% AR inversion yielded 95.2% minimum coverage across zero-strength ProxyGrid-v1 cells.
Intersect 97.5% ProxyLP-v1 and 97.5% AR sets using TV slack 10δ under |bridge|≤5; certify narrowing through endpoint margins.
With TV slack 10δ and |bridge|≤5, intersecting 97.5% LP/AR sets covers ≥95% uniformly; either component’s positive endpoint margin narrows bounds.
Simulate 97.5% ProxyLP-v1/AR intersections with |bridge|≤5, 10δ slack, strengths 0–0.2, δ≤0.05; assess minimum coverage and endpoint-margin tightening.
At overlap 0.2 and δ=0.05, weighted AR drift reached 0.63, exceeding 10δ=0.50; intersection coverage fell to 93.1%.
What overlap-dependent slack bounds weighted AR drift under TV violations δ≤0.05 and |bridge|≤5?
Derive overlap-dependent TV dual-norm slack for weighted AR moments, then retest the δ=0.05, overlap-0.2 failure cell.
Derive overlap-dependent δ·osc(weighted score) slack; retest intersection coverage at overlap 0.2 and |bridge|≤5 zero-strength endpoint tightening.
At overlap 0.2, weighted-score clipping to oscillation ≤10 restored 95.2% minimum intersection coverage with 10δ slack and zero-strength tightening.
Adopt |bridge|≤5, oscillation-10 clipping, and 10δ slack for 97.5% intersections; unclipped weighting covered only 93.1%.
Prove oscillation-10 TV slack and ≥95% uniform coverage for clipped 97.5% LP/AR intersections (|bridge|≤5, overlap≥0.2, δ≤0.05, strengths 0–0.2).
ClippedIntersection-v1 proves ≥95% uniform coverage for intersected 97.5% sets under oscillation≤10, |bridge|≤5, overlap≥0.2, δ≤0.05, strengths 0–0.2.
Replace overlap-slack retesting with clipped LP/AR dual-margin thresholds for width<2.0; validate ClippedIntersection-v1 at zero strength, δ≤0.05.
Compute clipped LP/AR endpoint dual margins on zero-strength ProxyGrid-v1 cells across δ≤0.05; compare certified width against 2.0.
ClippedIntersection-v2 adds bilateral LP/AR dual-margin certificates for width<2.0 at zero strength and δ≤0.05, retaining v1’s uniform coverage conditions.
Develop Γ≤2 treatment-selection odds bounds with δ≤0.05 proxy-TV uncertainty, using simultaneous 95% bands to retain validity at zero proxy strength.
Can Γ≤2 selection restrictions yield width<2.0 at zero proxy strength when ClippedIntersection-v2 has no positive dual margins?
At treatment propensity 0.5 and Γ≤2, selection-only LP yields width<2.0 for binary outcomes despite zero proxy strength and δ≤0.05.
On ProxyGrid-v1 zero-strength, zero-margin cells, solve 95%-band TV-robust Γ≤2 LP at propensity 0.5; test coverage and width<2.0 across δ≤0.05.
At propensity 0.5 and δ=0.05, Γ=2 LP retained width 2.0 in 24% of zero-strength, zero-margin cells; coverage ≥95.1%.
At zero proxy strength, Γ≤2 and δ≤0.05 yield width<2.0 if both arms’ 95%-band-adjusted outcome probabilities lie within [0.2,0.8].
Derive Γ=2 armwise LP width bounds under band-adjusted outcomes in [0.2,0.8]; validate δ≤0.05, zero-strength cells.
Select ClippedIntersection-v2-certified zero-margin cells with band-adjusted arm probabilities in [0.2,0.8]; test Γ=2 LP width<2.0 and coverage at zero strength, δ≤0.05.
GammaSelection-v1 tabulates Γ=2 LP widths and coverage for zero-strength, zero-margin cells with band-adjusted arm probabilities in [0.2,0.8].
Audit GammaSelection-v1 for width<2.0 and ≥95% coverage; derive Γ=2 endpoint certificates for arm probabilities in [0.2,0.8].
GammaSelection-v1: all qualifying cells had width≤1.84 and minimum coverage 95.2%; Γ=2 armwise LP certificates excluded both outcome-range endpoints.
Gate Γ=2 tightening on both band-adjusted arm probabilities in [0.2,0.8]: qualifying widths≤1.84, while ungated cells can retain width 2.0.
Benchmark GammaSelection-v1 against ProxyLP-v1 on matched zero-strength cells; compare minimum coverage, median width, and endpoint exclusion across δ≤0.05.
On matched qualifying zero-strength cells, GammaSelection-v1 median width was 1.62 versus ProxyLP-v1’s 1.89; minimum coverage was 95.2% versus 95.1%.
Prefer Γ=2 bounds when [0.2,0.8]-gated (median width 1.62 versus 1.89); otherwise retain εK-inflated LP; separately report certified clipped intersections.
